title: Doc's Sports AI-v3 Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: Doc's Sports AI-v3 review, checked 20 Nov 2026: $89 to $595 prices, refund terms, and five archived copies of its profit claims compared.
dek: An "artificial intelligence" pick feed sold by Doc's Sports, sent by text message for $89 for 3 days, $195 a week or $595 a month. The page now claims +25,460 profit since inception. It shows no pick log and no unit size, and the product has been renamed from v1 to v2 to v3 while one running total carried on. Its own totals show a strong first half of 2026 and a near flat summer.

status.label: Not verified

short_answer: Doc's Sports AI-v3 is a real product from one of the oldest names in the pick selling business. Doc's Sports says it has operated since 1971, names Doc's Enterprises in Sauk City, Wisconsin as the operator, prints the prices, and says picks arrive by text message, 1 to 4 messages a day per service. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Whether the model makes money is a different question, and nothing we could open answers it. On 20 Nov 2026 the page claimed "+25,460 Profit Since Inception!" and "+20,900 Profit So Far 2026!!", but it shows no picks, no odds, no post times and no unit size. We compared six dated copies of the page from October 2025 to today. The totals add up from copy to copy, which is to the seller's credit, and they show that most of the 2026 profit was claimed before mid June. Between 12 Jun and 7 Nov the total grew by less than the October figure alone.

We found no independent buyer who has written about this product by name on any forum, review site or Reddit. Treat AI-v3 as a seller with marketing totals, not a proven model. If you buy, buy the 3 day package, log every text yourself with the line and the time it arrived, and judge it only after a few hundred picks.

guarantee: The AI-v3 page says nothing about a guarantee, and it did not in the archived AI-v1 and AI-v2 copies either. The general Doc's terms say: "Once a product or service has been purchased and delivered or viewed, there are no refunds." They add that a guarantee is "usually the result of incorrect predictions in which case individual accounts will get extended for an additional period of time", that one day packages may get a credit, and that "All other services and packages will be reviewed and accounts will be extended at the sole discretion of the staff at Doc's Sports."

So for a 3 day, weekly or monthly AI-v3 package, the most a losing buyer can expect from the written terms is an extension that staff may or may not grant. We found no cash refund terms and no automatic renewal terms on the pages we opened. The terms also say Doc's is "not liable for any losses that are incurred as a result of the information purchased", and that "There have been no promises, guarantees or warranties suggesting that any bet or gamble will result in a profit". Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and at 1 to 4 texts a day those losses can be much larger than the package price.

The SMS terms add that "message and data rates may apply" and that "Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages." A pick that arrives late, after the line has moved, still counts the same in the seller's totals.

claims_note: How we checked. The page has no pick log, so we used the only record the seller does publish: its own running totals. We read six dated copies of the page, four saved by the Wayback Machine (7 Oct 2025, 18 Jan 2026, 17 Feb 2026, 12 Jun 2026) and two we opened ourselves (7 Nov and 20 Nov 2026), and lined up the figures.

The totals are consistent with each other. The February 2026 copy says "+4,560 Final Profit in 2025!!", "+6,990 Profit So Far 2026!!" and "+11,550 Profit Since Inception!", and 4,560 plus 6,990 is 11,550. Today's +25,460 since inception minus +20,900 in 2026 also leaves 4,560. So the "since inception" figure includes results sold under the AI-v1 name in 2025, before AI-v3 existed, and the seller has not rewritten the 2025 number between copies.

Lined up by date, the seller's own 2026 figures read: about +1,140 by 18 Jan (5,700 since inception less 4,560), +6,990 by 17 Feb, +15,735 by 12 Jun, +18,620 by 7 Nov and +20,900 by 20 Nov. That is roughly +8,745 between mid February and mid June, then only +2,885 between 12 Jun and 7 Nov. October alone is claimed at +3,450, so by the seller's own numbers the rest of that span, mid June through September plus the first week of November, lost about 565 taken together. The page now counts nine winning months out of ten; in June it said there had been no losing month yet, so the one losing month fell in the summer. Since 7 Nov the claimed total has risen again by 2,280 in 13 days.

The page never explains what the numbers measure. Doc's figures like this usually mean dollars of profit for a bettor risking $100 per unit, but the AI page does not say so, and it shows no unit size, no odds and no count of picks. One clue: the member notes say AI-v3 "went 0-1 on Thursday for -420", so a single losing pick cost 420 of these points. Without knowing the stake behind each pick, a buyer cannot turn +25,460 into a return on money risked.
record: Watchdog search, 22 Nov 2026: we searched about 1.37 million captured public posts from X, Reddit, Covers, TheRX and other forums for Doc's Sports AI-v3 plays that were posted or reposted before a game started. We found none, so there is no Watchdog graded sample for this seller yet.

Independently verifiable: nothing we found. We found no time stamped log of every AI pick held by a third party, no contest run by someone else, and no regulator or court record about results. For some of its human handicappers Doc's newsletters link "documented" play by play logs; we found no such log linked for the AI product, and the AI feed was not mentioned in the Doc's newsletters we read from November 2025 and late October 2026.

Seller's own marketing: running profit totals on the AI page and on the homepage roster, a monthly total for October, a count of winning months and member notes such as "AI-v3 went 0-1 on Thursday for -420". None of these lists the picks, the odds or the post times, so a buyer cannot rebuild them.

What we can check is the history of the claims. Wayback Machine copies show the page as AI-v1 on 7 Oct 2025 ("70% ALL SPORTS RUN (+4,250)"), still AI-v1 on 18 Jan 2026 ("+5,700 Profit Since Inception"), headed AI-v2 on 17 Feb 2026 with an AI-v1 bio underneath ("+11,550 Profit Since Inception"), AI-v2 on 12 Jun 2026 ("+20,295 Profit Since Inception", with "+19,595" further down the same page), and AI-v3 in November 2026. The name changed twice and the bio wording was softened; the record behind it was never published.

our_data.text: In this edition no Doc's Sports AI-v3 pick feed is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its picks perform.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Doc's Sports AI-v3 is close to nonexistent. We found no review, forum thread or Reddit post that discusses the AI product by name. What exists is about Doc's Sports in general.

customers.text: After searching Covers, Sportsbook Review, TheRX, Reddit, Sitejabber, Trustpilot and PissedConsumer, we found no buyer who has written about the AI product by name, in any year. The posts we did find are about Doc's Sports as a whole. A 2025 to 2026 TheRX thread is split between a long time customer asking for feedback and a member who said Doc's sellers show hot runs and hide cold streaks. A 2014 Sportsbook Review thread has members saying Doc's big plays tend to lose. Sitejabber rates Doc's 1.8 of 5 from 12 reviews, none about the AI feed. There is no smoke here either way, only silence, so the seller's own totals are the only evidence and nobody outside Doc's has checked them.

The "Member Notes" box on the AI-v3 page is written by Doc's, not by buyers. On 20 Nov 2026 it reported the running totals, a 0-1 Thursday for -420, and that the feed was "looking for 10 of 11 winning months". It tells you what the seller wants to highlight, not what a typical buyer experienced.

In a TheRX thread about Doc's Sports in general, a member said Doc's handicappers highlight hot runs and hide cold streaks, that they track the plays the day after, and that some sellers are worth betting against. The thread does not mention the AI product, they posted no log, and we did not verify their claims.
The same TheRX thread was opened by a bettor who said they had used Doc's Sports off and on for more than 10 years and asked others for feedback. Nobody in the thread mentioned the AI feed.

Long before the AI product, members of a Sportsbook Review thread about a Doc's handicapper said Doc's big plays in general tend to lose, and one said fading Doc's plays had made them about 17 units. This is about the house's human sellers, not the AI feed, and no record was posted.

Web searches of Covers, TheRX and SBR for Doc's Sports AI found no discussion of the product, and the Reddit posts we searched never mention it. Trustpilot listed no reviews of docsports.com when we checked on 7 Nov 2026, and the 12 Sitejabber reviews and one PissedConsumer review of Doc's that we read never mention the AI product. There is no app to rate, since picks arrive by text message.

conflicts: The Doc's FAQ says: "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in. We suggest that you give a couple of these a try." On 20 Nov 2026 the free pick on the Doc's homepage listed its line as "Offered at: BookMaker". A seller that steers readers to particular sportsbooks may have a financial interest in their betting, whatever the picks do.
Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Check the law where you live before you follow that advice.

AI-v3 is a house product of Doc's Sports, sold beside its human handicappers and other text services such as Doc's Consensus Picks, advertised at 2 to 6 picks a day by text. Doc's both runs the model and publishes the only numbers about it, and it chooses when to rename it.
strengths: A named operator, a mailing address, a toll free phone line, an email address and printed prices.
Short packages exist. A buyer can test it for 3 days at $89 before paying $595 for a month.
The running totals add up across six dated copies of the page, so the seller is at least not rewriting old totals from one copy to the next.
The page dropped its old line that the model would "virtually guarantee a winning edge", which is a step toward plainer marketing.
Delivery terms are written down: text messages, 1 to 4 per day per service, with message and data rates possible.
concerns: No public pick log. Every number is a seller total with no picks, odds, post times or unit size.
"Since inception" includes results from earlier versions sold under the AI-v1 and AI-v2 names.
By the seller's own figures, most of the 2026 profit was claimed before mid June, and the span from mid June to early November outside October lost money.
No guarantee is stated for AI-v3, and the site terms rule out refunds once picks are delivered.
The marketing leans on claims nobody can check, such as betting ticket data it says not to ask about.
No independent buyer has written about the product anywhere we could find, so there is no outside view at all.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A running profit total is not a record.
Ask what one unit is worth in the totals and how many units each pick risks. Without that, +25,460 cannot be turned into a return.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. For AI-v3 none is stated, and the site terms rule out refunds.
Write down each text the moment it arrives, with the time and the line you can actually get. Lines move fast on model picks.
Give any model or handicapper a few hundred picks before you call it a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real product sold by Doc's Enterprises, a long running pick seller with a named address and printed prices. We could not verify that the model wins over time, because Doc's publishes only profit totals and no log of the picks.
How much does Doc's Sports AI-v3 cost?
On 20 Nov 2026 the AI-v3 page listed $89.00 for 3 days, $195.00 for a week and $595.00 for 30 days, with picks sent by text message. The prices were the same in February 2026.
Does Doc's Sports AI-v3 have a verified record?

No. The page claims +25,460 since inception and +20,900 in 2026, but shows no picks, odds, post times or unit size, and we found no third party log or audit. The total also carries over results sold under the AI-v1 and AI-v2 names.
Is Doc's Sports AI-v3 the same as AI-v1 and AI-v2?
Doc's sells it as a new version each time, but the page kept one running profit total through all three names and much of the same wording. We cannot tell from outside what changed in the model.
Does Doc's Sports AI-v3 give refunds?
The AI page states no guarantee, and the Doc's terms say there are no refunds once a product is delivered or viewed. Any extension is at the staff's discretion.
Is Doc's Sports AI-v3 worth it?

You get 1 to 4 text messages a day of model picks across sports, at about $20 to $30 a day. What is unproven is the edge itself: the only evidence is the seller's own totals, which by their own numbers include a near flat summer, and no money comes back if the picks lose.
